Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the ShopNova Inc. Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question during the Q&A, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. There will be an instruction following the announcement. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to ShopNova's Q3 earnings call. Joining me today are Jamie Chen, CEO; Michael Patel, CFO; Sarah Lopez, COO; and David Kim, CMO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jamie Chen, CEO of ShopNova.

Jamie Chen:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q3 performance, driven by robust marketplace momentum and effective personalization technologies alongside targeted marketing initiatives. We saw significant growth in key metrics like GMV and revenue, reflecting our ability to navigate macroeconomic challenges.

Our focus remains on enhancing our Flywheel 2.0 strategy with AI-driven dynamic pricing and supply chain optimizations. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our NovaRecs version 4.2 recommendation engine, which we believe will significantly boost conversion rates through hyper-personalized bundles.

We are investing heavily in expanding Fulfillment by ShopNova into new categories like electronics and beauty.

Finally, we are committed to disciplined marketing execution that drives brand awareness and efficient customer acquisition.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Patel, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Michael Patel:
Thank you, Jamie. Our Q3 revenue was $20.8 billion, an increase of 14.3% year-over-year from $18.2 billion in Q3 2023 and 6.7% quarter-over-quarter from $19.5 billion in Q2 2024. This marks our strongest quarterly top-line beat in two years, exceeding our guidance range of 12-14% YoY growth by 140 basis points at the midpoint. We guided conservatively back in July amid macroeconomic headwinds like persistent U.S. inflation around 3% and softening consumer sentiment indexes, such as the Conference Board at 103.8 for September. We anticipated a cautious back-to-school season and early holiday ramp-up, especially with low-cost disruptors like Temu and Shein capturing share in apparel and home goods. But our execution across personalization tech, supply chain efficiencies, and targeted marketing campaigns turned those risks into tailwinds, delivering $250 million more revenue than the high end of our guide.

Breaking it down by segment highlights our diversification and resilience. Marketplace revenue, now 62% of total at $12.9 billion, grew 16.8% YoY and 8.2% QoQ, driven by a 12% increase in Gross Merchandise Value to $45.2 billion. This was powered by NovaRecs version 4.2, which boosted conversion rates by 18% via hyper-personalized bundles, similar to Amazon Prime Day lifts. Active sellers reached a record 2.1 million, up 22% YoY, thanks to our Fulfillment by ShopNova program expanding to 15 new categories, including electronics and beauty.

First-party retail revenue at $5.6 billion grew 11.2% YoY and 4.9% QoQ, slightly below internal expectations due to inventory optimization amid freight costs up 7% from Red Sea disruptions. Average Order Value held steady at $48, supported by premium private-label launches like our NovaHome smart kitchen line, which saw 35% uptake in upsell cross-sells.

Advertising and other revenue, our high-margin engine at $2.3 billion or 11% of total, surged 22.4% YoY and 9.1% QoQ. Sponsored products on search and feed pages mirrored Meta's ad auction dynamics, with RPMs up 15% to $4.20, as brands like Procter & Gamble and Unilever doubled down on shoppable video ads ahead of Black Friday.

Regionally, North America, 75% of revenue at $15.6 billion, delivered 15.1% YoY growth, beating our 13% guide thanks to same-day delivery penetration reaching 28% in urban hubs via 150 new micro-fulfillment centers, echoing Ocado's automation playbook. U.S. consumer spending on discretionary goods rebounded, per Adobe Analytics showing e-commerce up 9% in Q3.

EMEA at $3.2 billion grew 13.7% YoY despite VAT headwinds, via Brexit-proofed cross-border logistics, with Germany and UK GMV up 19% on localized flash sales akin to Zalando's model.

APAC and LatAm combined at $2.0 billion rose 18.2% YoY, led by India hitting 50 million monthly active users post-JioMart partnership. Brazil's Pix payment integration drove 25% AOV lift despite currency volatility.

These results validate our Flywheel 2.0 initiative: layering AWS SageMaker-driven dynamic pricing on supply chain AI reduced stockouts by 24%, contributing 300 basis points to YoY growth. Subscription momentum with NovaPrime members growing 14% to 145 million, ARPU up 8% from perks like grocery ultrafast delivery, positions us against Walmart+ and Instacart.

Before moving on, let me touch on our marketplace fee structure updates from early Q2, a key strategic lever influencing seller economics on our platform with over 2.5 million active sellers and $45 billion trailing twelve-month GMV. Our fee model includes referral fees averaging 14.2%, fulfillment via Fulfillment by ShopNova, ad auctions, and services like ShopNova Stores.

We shifted to tiered referral fees: 10-12% for Prime Eligible sellers with 98%+ on-time delivery and 4.5+ star ratings; 15-18% for standard; 20%+ penalty for underperformers below 95%. GFS fee rebates up to 25% for $1M+ annual GMV sellers, dynamic pricing for oversized items reducing inbound fees by 8%. Ad CPC floors lowered 15% for premium listings, plus a Fee Optimizer AI tool in Seller Central.

Data-driven from seller cohort analysis benchmarking Amazon's FBA hikes and Walmart's tiers, this aligned incentives with buyer expectations, boosting take rate from 22.1% in Q1 to 23.8% in Q3.

Impact on seller behavior exceeded models: net active sellers up 7% to 2.67 million; low-performer churn down 18% to 11.6% QoQ as 42,000 upgraded or exited; high-volume Professional sellers grew 12% to 28% of base.

GFS penetration surged 15% to 62% of units, cutting logistics COGS 9% as % of GMV; mid-tier adoption jumped from 45% to 58%.

Advertising from sellers up 22% YoY to $1.2 billion, ad spend as % of seller revenue up 17% to 4.2%; Fee Optimizer drove 31% more optimized listings, 6% GMV uplift, AOV up 4% to $52.

Sellers pivoted to higher-margin categories—electronics/home goods up 5% to 35% share; private-label launches up 14% to 22% of top-10K SKUs; dynamic pricing adoption up 25%.

In North America (55% GMV), GFS adoption lifted 18%, same-day units to 28%, gaining 2.5 points electronics share to 19%. APAC (28%) rebounded 11% post-Optimizer; EMEA/LATAM (17%) saw 9-12% shifts.

This reinforces our flywheel: buyer NPS up 3 to 87, LTV +7% to $142, CAC stable at $28. Piloting Advanced Tier with blockchain sustainability for 20% premium pricing.

Take rate expansion sustainable, seller ARPU up 11% to $17K, delivering $280 million incremental Q3 profit—8% ahead of guide.

Gross margin was 42.5%, driven by scale in advertising and GFS efficiencies offsetting freight pressures. Operating expenses were $8.5 billion, representing 41% of revenue. Our sales and marketing spend of $285 million rose 12% YoY but delivered strong efficiency.

Net income for the quarter was $1.2 billion, or $0.85 per share. We ended the quarter with $15 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are raising our full-year guidance to $85-88 billion in revenue, with Q4 at $24.5-25.5 billion implying 13-17% YoY growth, reflecting holiday acceleration and $2 billion capex in robotics warehousing.

Now I'll turn it over to Sarah Lopez to discuss operations.

Sarah Lopez:
Thanks, Michael. Operationally, we focused on supply chain density and tech-enabled logistics. Our shipping times improved by 25%, with same-day delivery now at 28% in key markets. Fulfillment costs were down 12% as a percentage of GMV through AI-optimized robotic picking in 25 new facilities and GFS rebates. We are implementing ShopSphere Live interactive livestream shopping, generating $1.2 billion GMV up 150% QoQ.

These efforts, including micro-warehouses for under-2-hour delivery in 40 metros and partnerships like DoorDash, directly supported our GMV growth to $50.8 billion total—marketplace at $45.2 billion up 28% YoY and 12% QoQ from $23.6 billion in Q2, beating 25-27% YoY guidance by 110 basis points. Annual active buyers hit 185 million up 22% YoY, repeat rates 68% up 8%, AOV $145 up 5%, frequency 3.8 up 2%.

U.S./North America $13.7 billion up 24%, APAC $7.4 billion up 42% via India UPI, Europe $4.0 billion up 18%. Onboarded 250,000 new sellers, catalog to 1.2 billion SKUs; BNPL like Klarna upped cart completion 20%; B2B added $800 million.

Now I'll turn it over to David Kim.

David Kim:
Thanks, Sarah. From a marketing perspective, we saw strong results from our Wave of Innovation campaign and TikTok Shop integrations. Customer acquisition costs were $42.30, down 7% QoQ and 19% YoY from $52.10, with ROAS at 5.1x above our 4x threshold.

Brand awareness surged: Nielsen aided recall up 32% YoY to 68% in U.S., Google Trends +45%; $120 million Q3 spend—40% performance, 30% CTV/YouTube, 30% social. TikTok micro-influencers hit 150 million impressions, 7.2x ROAS, 2.5 million visits. Snapchat/Pinterest boosted Europe unaided awareness 24%.

Added 1.8 million net new customers, 22% YoY, new AOV $85 up 15% QoQ. Blended CAC $42 via multi-touch attribution, server-side tagging reducing signal loss 35%, incrementality to 28%. AI DCO on Meta 4.8x ROAS; Klaviyo email/SMS 42% open, $0.18 rev/email.

North America 25% new growth, CTV 18% SOV; APAC 48% via JioMart/Shopee, CAC $28; Europe 12% with Trade Desk. LTV/CAC 3.8x, 24-month retention 52%.

ROAS breakdown: Google 6.8x, Meta 4.2x, TikTok 7.2x; SEO +22% organic to 45%; affiliates sub-$15 CAC. ML bidding cut waste 22%, gen AI creatives +15% CTR. Q4 CAC $41-43, ROAS 5.3x.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to ask a question, please press star one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from John Smith with JPMorgan.

John Smith:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Jamie, can you elaborate on the key drivers behind the revenue beat and how sustainable this is into Q4 amid holiday competition?

Jamie Chen:
Thanks, John. Absolutely, the revenue beat stemmed from marketplace outperformance at 16.8% YoY on $45.2 billion GMV, fueled by NovaRecs conversions up 18% and seller growth to 2.1 million via FBS expansion. Ad revenue +22.4% as brands ramped shoppable videos. Regionally, NA same-day delivery and APAC partnerships like JioMart were pivotal. Sustainability into Q4 looks strong with raised guidance to $24.5-25.5 billion, holiday capex in robotics, and Fed rate cuts boosting spend—though monitoring China stimulus pricing effects. Our Flywheel 2.0 derisks this.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Johnson with Goldman Sachs.

Emily Johnson:
Great, thanks. Michael, on GMV—$50.8 billion total beat nicely, but how much came from fee updates versus organic buyer growth, and any update to FY guide?

Michael Patel:
Emily, thanks. Total GMV $50.8 billion up 28% YoY/12% QoQ beat 25-27% guide, validating execution despite inflation in apparel/electronics. AABs +22% to 185 million, Prime 120 million driving 55% GMV; AOV +5% to $145 via Nexus ML cross-sells +22%. Fee updates contributed via seller quality—GFS to 62%, optimized listings +31% adding 6% uplift—but core from buyer retention 68% and Live generating $1.2 billion. FY guide raised to $102-105 billion GMV, 27-29% YoY; Q4 30%+ on holidays/Live to 20% GMV. FX/tariffs noted, but 65/35 seller mix helps.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Lee with Morgan Stanley.

Mike Lee:
Thanks. Sarah, fulfillment costs improved sharply—can you talk logistics investments and seller response to GFS rebates, any bottlenecks ahead?

Sarah Lopez:
Mike, shipping times down 25%, costs -12% via $500 million AI fulfillment in 25 facilities, free shipping at $35 AOV. GFS rebates drove 15% penetration surge to 62%, mid-tier from 45-58%; sellers love it for Prime speeds. North America +18% adoption countered Amazon; APAC rebounded post-monsoon. No major bottlenecks—150 micro-centers scaling, robotics capex for Q4 peak. Ties to stockouts -24%, directly +300 bps growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Barclays.

Lisa Chen:
Congrats team. David, CAC efficiency impressive at $42—how are you navigating privacy changes, and outlook for ROAS in holiday with election volatility?

David Kim:
Lisa, thanks. CAC $42.30 down 19% YoY on 4.2 million new customers, LTV:CAC 4.2x with $312 cohort LTV. Privacy via server-side tagging/first-party clean rooms cut signal loss 35%, SKAdNetwork 4.0 accuracy +18%; cookieless 35% now. ROAS 5.1x: Google 6.8x, TikTok 7.2x Gen Z AOV +2.5x. Holiday: pre-sales 1.8x lift, AR try-ons +28% conv, CTV ramp to 3.5x; expect 5.3x despite CPMs, 20-25% new growth on $150 million spend.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Jamie Chen for closing remarks.

Jamie Chen:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
